desc: Derive the exact visibility condition: building i invisible from (0,h) iff h ≤ max over j<i of y-intercept b_{ij} = (H_j·X_i − H_i·X_j)/(X_i − X_j); grazing counts as blocking (confirmed by Samples 1 and 3).
Prove the reduction: best visible target is the top (X_i,H_i); answer = max(0, max_i b_i), output −1 iff max_i b_i < 0; answer 0 when max b_i = 0 (Sample 3).
Implement upper convex hull (monotone chain, integer cross products) over points (X_i,H_i) inserted in increasing X order.
Implement tangent query: binary search hull for vertex maximizing intercept with (X_i,H_i), comparing intercepts exactly via cross-multiplication.
Track global max t_i as exact rational (num, den) with cross-multiplication comparisons; skip i=1.
Implement I/O and output: if best num < 0 print -1 exactly, else print max(0, num/den) with ~15 decimals.
Validate against the four samples and stress-test hull tangent logic against O(N²) brute force on random small cases (collinear points, equal heights, -1/0 edge cases).
